name: HP SitePrint
summary: A small wheeled robot that prints wall lines, openings and other layout from a CAD file onto the slab, guided by a robotic total station.

priceEur.note: Robot price reported by trade press in April 2024 (Allsat demo); monthly usage fees come on top, capped at EUR 12,000 or 10,000 m² per month. Confirm current price with the seller.

sellers.note: Listed by HP as sales partner for Germany. Sells and rents (weekly or monthly billing, price on request).
sellers.name: ALLSAT GmbH

sellers.note: Listed by HP as sales partner for Germany; product 26101000, price not shown.
sellers.name: Gottlieb Nestle GmbH

germany.statusNote: HP lists Allsat (Hannover) and Gottlieb Nestle (Dornstetten) as its sales partners for Germany; Allsat also rents it out. No public price; HP adds an area-based fee for software, service and ink.

specs.label: Marking accuracy
specs.conditions: average layout tolerance at 5-30 m, with the HP SMR prism in high-accuracy mode and a 1" total station (HP footnote)

specs.label: Accuracy over distance
specs.conditions: at 5-30 m from the total station (seller data sheet)

specs.label: Obstacle it can cross
specs.conditions: FAQ answer on rough concrete; another FAQ answer on the same page says up to 5 cm

specs.label: Runtime per battery
specs.conditions: per battery, continuous printing; two batteries included, together about one working day

specs.label: Swappable battery
specs.conditions: two Li-ion batteries in the box

specs.label: Compatible total stations
specs.value: Leica TS16, TS60, iCON iCR80, iCR70; Topcon LN-150, GT-600, GT-1200; Trimble RTS 573, S9

notes: Needs a robotic total station (bought separately) with continuous line of sight to the prism on the robot.
Prints on concrete, asphalt, plywood, pavers, terrazzo, vinyl and epoxy; the HP FAQ gives obstacle crossing as 2 cm in one answer and 5 cm in another.
Stairs set to false because it is a small floor robot that is carried between levels; no source mentions stairs.
Version 3.0 upgrade adds depth-camera obstacle avoidance and up to 30% more speed.
Works on damp floors but not in puddles or rain (HP FAQ); keeps about 20 cm from walls according to the 2024 German demo report.

images.alt: HP SitePrint layout robot with prism on top, side view

evidence.task: Printed layout and floor levelness points for server rack installation (about 4,500 anchor positions) in a data centre
evidence.where: Redman Robotics, data centre (country not named; the US case study gives the area as 120,000 sq ft)
evidence.note: HP case study; not shown to be a German project.

evidence.task: Printed the floor plan on site for a police station under construction (demo by Allsat)
evidence.where: Gottfried Stehnke Bauunternehmung, Polizeirevier Geestemünde, Bremerhaven, Germany
evidence.note: Demo was moved indoors because of rain; Allsat was then the exclusive German distributor.

evidence.task: Printed wall, partition, sprinkler and electrical layouts on two projects (12,000 m²)

Marked about 24,000 m² of layout in one month on one project and over 48,000 m² in total, mostly drywall layouts in hospitals and industrial buildings; the firm says two people need five to six days to mark the same drywall layout by hand, the robot about one day
evidence.note: Statements by the user in a story by the German distributor Allsat, published 2 June 2026.
